chapter: 06. Multiple Sclerosis & Other CNS Demyelinating Disorders
countBasis: One question per distinct high-yield diagnostic or therapeutic decision. This provisional 44-decision map reflects clinical breadth, not an official examination weighting. Final editorial review may add missing decisions or remove overlap.

decisions: Recognize a typical clinically isolated syndrome and exclude nonspecific symptoms
Distinguish characteristic MS lesion morphology from vascular white-matter disease
Identify the five dissemination-in-space regions in the 2024 revisions
Interpret CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands and the kappa free-light-chain alternative
Apply the four-or-five-region diagnostic pathway in a typical clinical presentation
Demonstrate MRI dissemination in time with new or simultaneous enhancing and nonenhancing lesions
Apply the adult select-6 central-vein-sign rule and its fewer-than-ten-lesion qualification
Use a paramagnetic rim lesion with the necessary accompanying evidence in single-region disease
Apply the unified progressive-onset pathway with at least twelve months of progression
Demand additional specificity in older patients or those with vascular comorbidity
Interpret the updated radiologically isolated presentation pathway without assuming every incidental lesion is MS
Distinguish disease activity from progression in MS phenotype descriptors
Distinguish infection-associated pseudorelapse from a new inflammatory attack
Choose an evidence-based high-dose methylprednisolone regimen for a disabling relapse
Escalate a severe steroid-refractory demyelinating attack to plasma exchange
Select an individualized high-efficacy strategy for highly active relapsing disease
Recognize ocrelizumab evidence in primary progressive MS and the population limitation
Screen for hepatitis B and plan vaccination before anti-CD20 therapy
Stratify natalizumab-associated PML risk using JCV status, exposure and prior immunosuppression
Plan a monitored transition from fingolimod to minimize rebound disease
Recognize S1P-modulator cardiac and macular safety requirements
Use accelerated teriflunomide elimination in the appropriate reproductive context
Respond to persistent severe lymphopenia during dimethyl fumarate treatment
Apply cladribine pregnancy, infection and vaccination precautions
Match interferon beta and glatiramer acetate mechanisms and safety to a treatment context
Apply AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD diagnostic requirements using a cell-based assay
Apply stricter seronegative NMOSD criteria and MRI requirements
Recognize area postrema syndrome and its dorsal medullary correlate
Differentiate AQP4 myelitis from typical MS and MOG-associated myelitis
Use early apheresis for a severe NMOSD attack with inadequate steroid response
Distinguish C5, CD19 and IL-6 receptor preventive therapeutic targets
Plan meningococcal risk mitigation before complement inhibition
Avoid MS therapies that can fail or worsen AQP4-positive NMOSD
Interpret a low-positive serum MOG-IgG result using the 2023 criteria
Recognize the anterior optic-neuritis and perineural enhancement phenotype
Recognize conus involvement and the gray-matter H-sign in MOG myelitis
Recognize unilateral cortical encephalitis with seizures and exclude infection
Distinguish ADEM with encephalopathy from a typical first MS attack
Treat acute MOGAD and individualize the steroid taper to relapse risk
Interpret maintenance IVIG evidence without claiming randomized superiority or universal need after one attack
Evaluate an open-ring tumefactive lesion while retaining tumour and infection in the differential
Recognize concentric demyelination as a radiological pattern rather than an automatic separate etiology
Select symptom-directed treatment for spasticity while addressing reversible triggers
Apply dalfampridine seizure and renal contraindications for walking impairment

crossChapterBoundaries: Detailed infectious demyelination and PML diagnosis belong to the completed CNS infections chapter; this chapter tests DMT-related risk and response rather than repeating infection questions.
Seizure management is not repeated in the MOG cortical encephalitis item.
Optic neuritis comparisons remain focused on inflammatory demyelinating disease.
requiredFinalReview: Confirm each criterion against the original 2024 McDonald position paper published in 2025; label historical criteria explicitly.
Recheck current regulatory labels, exact doses, reproductive precautions and locally relevant approval limitations.
Verify the current MOGAD treatment evidence and approval status before wording maintenance questions.
Review all distractors for realistic competition and each explanation for standalone teaching value.
Do not install a partial draft or treat structural validation as independent clinical review.
